source.title: Benign, Tempered, or Catastrophic: A Taxonomy of Overfitting
source.authors: Neil Rohit Mallinar; James B. Simon; Amirhesam Abedsoltan; Parthe Pandit; Mikhail Belkin; Preetum Nakkiran

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures noise profiles for neural networks and kernel regression and reports how training noise and training-to-interpolation status affect asymptotic test error. Its noise-profile method differs from the listed versions' specific capacity, architecture, optimizer, batch, regularization, sharpness, and memorized-example tests.
record.gate_note: Own experiments test whether DNNs trained to interpolation generalize on natural-label data while fitting noisy labels, and compare that behavior with early stopping. The noise-profile test directly bears on V1's coexistence of interpolation and natural-label generalization, although it does not report random-label held-out accuracy. Kernel and other results address overfitting regimes but do not test the specific mechanisms in V2–V8.
record.test_reason: The neural-network noise profiles bear on V1: the same training procedures interpolate noisy labels and generalize on natural image tasks. Importantly, the noise sweeps include p=0.5 for binary classification and p=0.9 for ten classes, where labels carry no predictive information about the original class. The study does not directly evaluate held-out randomly assigned labels. Its asymptotic Bayes-optimality question is distinct from V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct: the tested interpolating DNNs show empirical evidence of tempered overfitting, whereas early-stopped networks show approximately benign fitting. These finite, moderate-size experiments suggest asymptotic behavior rather than prove it. The paper also derives a kernel-regression trichotomy under spectral and approximation assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: Studies asymptotic noise profiles across training sizes and label-noise levels, rather than measuring random-label fitting and held-out random-label accuracy in Zhang et al. or the specific interventions in V2–V8. Uses both natural image datasets and synthetic tasks; networks are generally trained without explicit regularization.
record.method_sensitivity: Training stage matters: early-stopped networks show benign profiles, while networks trained to interpolation show tempered profiles. The reported VGG-19 CINIC-10 result is based on one experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Interpolating classifiers retain noise-dependent excess test error as sample size increases, including on a synthetic constant-function task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation need not become Bayes optimal as sample size grows at fixed task dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: Early-stopped image classifiers approach benign fitting, while synthetic regression test error rises as training begins fitting noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training duration can determine whether noisy-data fitting is approximately benign or tempered.

record.problems: DNN evidence is entirely empirical; the paper notes datasets are at most moderate in size. Most plotted network results are not numerically tabulated in the supplied text. VGG-19 on CINIC-10 is a single experiment. The study injects label noise and does not measure held-out accuracy under random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No required findings omitted. Kernel-regression experiments and results are not extracted as rows because V1–V8 concern the listed neural-network behaviors and interventions, and no version covers the paper's kernel spectral trichotomy. Nearest-neighbor and cited prior-study examples in Sections 2.4 and 3 are not own experiments.

untested.parts: Direct held-out accuracy against independently randomized test labels; the original architectures and datasets as a matched replication. Numerical endpoint errors cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.
Width sweeps and test-error changes beyond the width needed for interpolation.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and interventions on local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: Neither excess risk above Bayes optimality nor improvement from early stopping challenges V1. V1 asserts coexistence of memorization capacity and generalization, not statistical consistency. The record overlooks that its maximal label-noise settings remove label information; however, evaluation uses clean test labels throughout.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels or report held-out accuracy under random labels; instead evaluates natural datasets with injected label noise and compares interpolating with early-stopped networks.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and the specified MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 one-hidden-layer ReLU setup.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected models or tests isolating local connectivity.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or optimizer tuning.
No batch-size comparison or large-batch generalization-gap test.
No dropout intervention or comparison with removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other measure ranking generalization gaps.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28 × 10
rows.operation_detail: Trained on binary CIFAR-10 with injected label noise to interpolation; measured clean-test classification error.

conditions.value: no weight decay, dropout, or other regularization techniques

rows.measure: Clean test classification error as a function of training label-flip probability; plotted noise profile.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over three independent runs (Appendix C.3); no numeric errors stated in text.
rows.note: Authors describe test error increasing with training noise and persisting at a nonzero asymptotic value as n grows. The figure gives the profile values.
rows.check: Qualitative evidence supports interpolation alongside natural-task generalization; numerical curve values are unavailable. The sweep includes the uninformative-label endpoint p=0.5. Binary CIFAR-10 excludes frog and horse, and training includes random horizontal flips.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28 × 10
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ten-class CIFAR-10 with injected label noise to interpolation; measured clean-test classification error.

conditions.value: no weight decay, dropout, or other regularization techniques

rows.measure: Clean test classification error as a function of training label-noise proportion; plotted noise profile.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over three independent runs (Appendix C.3); no numeric errors stated in text.
rows.note: The paper says this interpolating DNN does not approach Bayes optimality and exhibits tempered overfitting.
rows.check: The sweep includes p=0.9, where uniformly choosing an alternative class produces uninformative labels overall. Persistent excess error under intermediate noise does not qualify or contradict V1, which does not assert Bayes optimality.

rows.subject: MLP (3 × 1024)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a synthetic constant-function classification task with injected label flips to interpolation; measured test classification error.

conditions.value: Synthetic classification on S 9; constant ground-truth label

rows.measure: Test classification error as a function of training label-flip probability; plotted noise profile.
rows.uncertainty: Mean over five independent runs; no error bars stated for this figure.
rows.note: At large sample size, the paper reports that interpolating networks do not learn the constant function successfully in the presence of even slight label noise.
rows.check: Learning a synthetic constant label under label flips does not measure V1's natural-label image classification comparison. The default absence of explicit regularization applies here too.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28 × 10
rows.operation_detail: Trained on binary SVHN and selected early-stop epoch by two-fold cross-validation; measured clean-test classification error.

conditions.value: selected by validation classification error averaged over two folds; first ten epochs excluded

rows.measure: Clean test classification error as a function of training label noise; plotted noise profile.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over three independent runs; no numeric errors stated in text.
rows.note: Early-stopped networks approach zero test error as n increases, including at finite noise, but this is a different training stage than V1's recipe that fits random labels.
rows.check: Early stopping does not establish the coexistence of random-label interpolation and generalization required by V1. Appendix C.3 literally says the selected epoch maximizes validation classification error, conflicting with the main text's optimal-early-stopping description; the record should flag this apparent typo rather than silently resolve it.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28 × 10
rows.operation_detail: Trained on binary SVHN with injected label noise to interpolation; measured clean-test classification error.

conditions.value: no weight decay, dropout, or other regularization techniques

rows.measure: Clean test classification error as a function of training label noise; plotted noise profile.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over three independent runs; no numeric errors stated in text.
rows.note: The text says these noise profiles converge to a limiting, roughly linear curve as n increases.
rows.check: The listed sample sizes appear copied from Figure 6b. Figure 7's shared legend lists 9k, 18k, 36k and 70k. Its below-chance tempered classification error supports generalization despite interpolation; failure to reach Bayes optimality is not a V1 limitation.

rows.subject: VGG-19 with batch norm
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CINIC-10 with injected label noise; measured clean-test classification error.
rows.measure: Clean test classification error as a function of training label-flip probability; plotted noise profile.
rows.note: Authors report a tempered noise profile, but state they could run only one experiment due to computational limitations.
rows.check: The authors report a tempered profile for an overfit VGG on natural images. One experiment limits uncertainty assessment, not the effect's state. The default no-weight-decay/no-dropout setup applies. Numerical training accuracy and curve values are not supplied.

source_check.correct: Regularization: no weight decay, dropout or other regularization techniques under the default setup; no VGG-specific exception is stated.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix C.2 default setup; Appendix C.3 VGG setup; Figure 11; Appendix D.2.
source_check.problem: Regularization is recorded as unstated despite an applicable explicit default.

rows.subject: 3 × 1024 MLP
rows.stage_stated: trained until training loss ≤ 1 × 10−4; 100% training accuracy
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Binary MNIST with injected label noise; measured clean-test classification error.

conditions.value: Adam; batch size 256; five independent runs

rows.measure: Clean test classification error as a function of training label-flip probability; plotted noise profile.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over five independent runs; no numeric errors stated in text.
rows.note: The paper describes the interpolating MLP as tempered; this is not a random-label held-out accuracy measurement.
rows.check: The interpolating MLP reaches 100% training accuracy and has a tempered natural-image noise profile. The binary sweep includes uninformative labels at p=0.5. The default absence of explicit regularization applies.

source_check.correct: Regularization: no weight decay, dropout or other regularization techniques under the default setup. The stated Adam optimizer, batch size 256, five independent runs and training-loss threshold agree with Appendix C.3.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix C.2 default setup; Appendix C.3 Binary MNIST experiment; Figure 3; Section 2.4.
source_check.problem: Regularization is recorded as unstated despite an applicable explicit default.

rows.subject: 3 × 1024 MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Binary MNIST with injected label noise for one epoch; measured clean-test classification error.
rows.measure: Clean test classification error as a function of training label-flip probability; plotted noise profile.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over five independent runs; no numeric errors stated in text.
rows.note: The paper describes one-epoch MLPs as benign, contrasting them with the same-architecture MLP trained to interpolation.
rows.check: The one-epoch comparator does not establish random-label fitting. Its benign profile is neither an incomplete instance nor a failure of V1.

rows.subject: 4 × 512 ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained on synthetic noisy regression data on S 4; measured train and test MSE over optimization time.

conditions.value: Inputs sampled uniformly on S 4; targets yi = 1 + N(0, 1)

rows.measure: Train and test MSE as a function of optimization time.
rows.uncertainty: Mean over five trials; no uncertainty values stated.
rows.note: The authors report test loss initially near Bayes optimal, then rising as training fits noise, and settling above Bayes optimal at large t. Regression experiment, rather than the classification setup in V1.
rows.check: Synthetic constant-function regression with Gaussian noise does not measure V1's natural-label versus random-label classification behavior. Appendix C.3 specifies 4 × 512, while Figure 8's caption says 4 × 500; retain the discrepancy.

relation.reason: The study reports its own neural-network interpolation and clean-test results, including noise sweeps reaching uninformative training labels.

tranche.reason: Noise sweeps and training-size comparisons test interpolation alongside natural-task generalization using a different method from the original random-label comparison.

source_check.notes: Curve values remain figure-only; support is qualitative, without a separate held-out random-label accuracy measurement. The authors describe finite, moderate-size DNN experiments as evidence for asymptotic behavior.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Interpolating networks on Binary CIFAR-10, CIFAR-10, synthetic S 9 classification, Binary MNIST, and 0/1 SVHN
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that networks trained to interpolation have test error above Bayes optimal that persists or converges as sample size grows (R1, R2, R3, R5, R7). This supports coexistence of fitting noisy labels and non-chance natural-task generalization, but does not test random-label holdout accuracy.

reader_labels.condition: Early-stopped Binary SVHN and Binary MNIST MLPs; single-run VGG-19 on CINIC-10; synthetic noisy regression MLP over time
reader_labels.reason: Behavior depends on training stage, and the VGG result has only one run; these experiments do not establish V1's specific random-label held-out comparison (R4, R6, R8, R9).
